substantive_delta: A deterministic polynomial-time construction for every fixed delta and all graph inputs and binary-encoded f,k at the full PPT almost-linear-fault mixed-stretch tradeoff. The new joint regime choice uses f-dependent exact path representatives only when (f+d+1)^O(d) is polynomial, and DR multiplicative spanners when their extra density can be charged to the allowed fault factor; the PPT insertion-witness packing is verified for the actual partial scan.
why_nonroutine: No new representative-family, gap-cut or packing primitive is claimed. The substantive independent step is the complementary-regime construction theorem and its complete quantifier-preserving proof: a representative DP alone has nonuniform polynomial cost for unrestricted faults, while a purely multiplicative theorem alone has the wrong density/stretch combination in the remaining regime. The size proof also requires transfer to the actual sequence rather than containment in a complete greedy run. This removes the source construction's quasi-polynomial path-enumeration barrier for the entire frozen target, not an elementary restatement of its existential size theorem or a fixed-parameter corollary. Current bounded primary-source checks, including recent RPC work, found no equivalent complete combined result.
significance: The result makes a recent general-graph mixed-stretch vertex-fault spanner tradeoff uniformly constructible in deterministic polynomial time while keeping almost-linear fault overhead. That is a substantive algorithmic benefit in an established TCS problem. It does not improve existential size/stretch, optimize the polynomial exponent or establish a new broad primitive; the separate STOC assessment is conservatively working_paper.
